title: Numbers Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 22.

questions.question: Where did the children of Israel pitch their camp according to Numbers 22:1?
options: In the plains of Moab on this side Jordan by Jericho
In the wilderness of Sinai
Near the Red Sea
In the land of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: In the plains of Moab on this side Jordan by Jericho
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:1 states that the children of Israel pitched in the plains of Moab on this side Jordan by Jericho.

questions.question: Who was Balak the son of Zippor?
options: King of the Moabites
A prophet of Israel
Elder of Midian
A prince of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: King of the Moabites
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:4 explicitly states that Balak the son of Zippor was king of the Moabites at that time.

questions.question: Why was Moab afraid of the children of Israel?
options: Because they were many
Because they had weapons of war
Because they had a large army
Because they had a strong king
questions.correctAnswer: Because they were many
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:3 says Moab was sore afraid of the people because they were many.

questions.question: To whom did Balak send messengers to curse the children of Israel?
options: Balaam the son of Beor
Moses
Aaron
Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: Balaam the son of Beor
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:5 states that Balak sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor to call him.

questions.question: What was Balak's reason for asking Balaam to curse the Israelites?
options: Because they were too mighty for him
Because they had stolen his land
Because they had insulted him
Because they had broken a treaty
questions.correctAnswer: Because they were too mighty for him
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:6 records Balak's words asking Balaam to curse the people because they were too mighty for him.

questions.question: True or False: The elders of Moab and Midian came to Balaam with rewards of divination in their hand.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:7 states the elders of Moab and Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand and came to Balaam.

questions.question: What did Balaam tell the princes of Moab to do after the LORD refused to allow him to go with them?
options: Get you into your land
Stay with me another night
Prepare sacrifices
Go and wait for my word
questions.correctAnswer: Get you into your land
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:13 says Balaam told the princes of Balak to get into their land because the LORD refused to let him go with them.

questions.question: True or False: God told Balaam he could go with the men but must only speak the word He gives him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:20 records God telling Balaam that if the men come to call him, he should go with them but only speak the word God gives him.

questions.question: Which action happened first in Numbers 22?
options: The children of Israel pitched in the plains of Moab
Balak sent messengers to Balaam
Balaam refused to go with the princes of Moab
God spoke to Balaam about the men with him
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel pitched in the plains of Moab
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:1 shows Israel pitched first; sending messengers, Balaam's refusal, and God's speaking came afterward (vv.5, 13, 9).

questions.question: What did Balak offer Balaam to persuade him to come and curse Israel?
options: Very great honour and to do whatsoever he would say
A large army to protect him
A share of the land of Moab
A golden crown
questions.correctAnswer: Very great honour and to do whatsoever he would say
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:17 records Balak promising to promote Balaam to very great honour and do whatsoever he says.

questions.question: True or False: Balaam said he could do more or less than the word of the LORD his God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:18 states Balaam said he cannot go beyond the word of the LORD his God to do less or more.

questions.question: What did Balaam request from the princes of Moab before he received further instruction from the LORD?
options: To tarry there this night
To return to Balak immediately
To build an altar
To prepare sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: To tarry there this night
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:19 says Balaam asked the princes to tarry that night so he might know what the LORD would say more.

questions.question: Who asked Balaam, 'What men are these with thee?'?
options: The LORD
Balak
The elders of Moab
The angel of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:9 says God came to Balaam and asked, 'What men are these with thee?'.

questions.question: True or False: Moab was confident that the Israelites would not overcome them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:3-4 explains Moab was sore afraid and distressed, fearing Israel would lick up all around them like oxen licking grass.

questions.question: What did the elders of Moab and Midian carry when they went to Balaam?
options: Rewards of divination
Weapons for protection
Scrolls of the law
Gifts of silver and gold
questions.correctAnswer: Rewards of divination
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:7 states that the elders departed with the rewards of divination in their hand and came to Balaam.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What reason did Balak give to Balaam for wanting him to curse Israel?
options: Because Israel was too mighty and he hoped to overcome them
Because Israel had stolen from Moab
Because Israel had broken a treaty
Because Israel worshiped false gods
questions.correctAnswer: Because Israel was too mighty and he hoped to overcome them
questions.explanation: Balak said Israel was too mighty for him and hoped that by Balaam cursing them, he might prevail and drive them out (Numbers 22:6). This is supported by Balak's fear and distress of Israel's power (Numbers 22:3).

questions.question: How did Balaam respond when first asked to come and curse Israel?
options: He refused because the LORD said not to go
He agreed immediately
He asked for a large payment
He cursed Israel right away
questions.correctAnswer: He refused because the LORD said not to go
questions.explanation: Balaam said the LORD refused to let him go with the men to curse Israel (Numbers 22:13), as God had told him not to curse the people because they were blessed (Numbers 22:12).

questions.question: What did Balak do after Balaam initially refused to come?
options: Sent more honorable princes to persuade Balaam
Gave up and sought another prophet
Attacked Israel directly
Sent gifts to Balaam's family
questions.correctAnswer: Sent more honorable princes to persuade Balaam
questions.explanation: After Balaam refused, Balak sent more princes, more honorable than the first, to try to persuade Balaam to come (Numbers 22:15).

questions.question: What did Balak promise Balaam if he would come and curse Israel?
options: Promotion to great honor and to do whatever he said
A large army to protect him
A share of the land
A permanent throne in Moab
questions.correctAnswer: Promotion to great honor and to do whatever he said
questions.explanation: Balak promised Balaam very great honor and that he would do whatever Balaam said if he would come and curse Israel (Numbers 22:17).

questions.question: How did Balaam demonstrate integrity in his answer to Balak's servants?
options: He said he could not go beyond God's word, even for great wealth
He demanded double the reward offered
He cursed Israel secretly
He agreed to curse Israel regardless of God's word
questions.correctAnswer: He said he could not go beyond God's word, even for great wealth
questions.explanation: Balaam stated that even if Balak gave him his house full of silver and gold, he could not do less or more than what the LORD said (Numbers 22:18), showing his obedience and integrity.

questions.question: What instruction did God give Balaam at night after the princes arrived again?
options: If the men come to call you, rise up and go, but only do what I tell you
Refuse to go under any circumstances
Curse Israel secretly without the princes knowing
Go and curse Israel immediately
questions.correctAnswer: If the men come to call you, rise up and go, but only do what I tell you
questions.explanation: God told Balaam that if the men come to call him, he should go with them but only do the word that God speaks to him (Numbers 22:20).

questions.question: What does Balaam saddling his ass and going with the princes teach us about obedience?
options: Obedience involves trusting God's instructions even when the situation is difficult
Obedience means doing whatever people ask regardless of God's word
Obedience is optional if rewards are low
Obedience means acting before seeking God's guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience involves trusting God's instructions even when the situation is difficult
questions.explanation: Balaam obeyed God’s instruction to go with the princes, showing trust in God's guidance despite the potential danger (Numbers 22:21), illustrating faithful obedience.

questions.question: Why was God's anger kindled against Balaam as he went with the princes?
options: Because Balaam went contrary to God's will or in a way not fully obedient
Because Balaam cursed Israel immediately
Because Balaam refused to eat with the princes
Because Balaam rebelled openly against God
questions.correctAnswer: Because Balaam went contrary to God's will or in a way not fully obedient
questions.explanation: God's anger was kindled because Balaam went, and the angel stood as adversary against him, implying Balaam's way was perverse before God (Numbers 22:22, 32).

questions.question: What caused Balaam's ass to turn aside from the path three times?
options: The ass saw the angel of the LORD with a drawn sword
The ass was tired and wanted to rest
The ass was frightened by wild animals
The ass wanted to find food
questions.correctAnswer: The ass saw the angel of the LORD with a drawn sword
questions.explanation: The ass turned aside because she saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way with a drawn sword (Numbers 22:23, 28).

questions.question: How did Balaam react to his ass's actions, and what does this teach about patience?
options: He struck the ass three times in anger, showing a lack of patience
He praised the ass for protecting him
He immediately stopped and prayed for guidance
He changed his route willingly
questions.correctAnswer: He struck the ass three times in anger, showing a lack of patience
questions.explanation: Balaam struck the ass three times in anger for turning aside, revealing his impatience before God opened his eyes (Numbers 22:23, 25, 27).

questions.question: What miraculous event occurred involving Balaam's ass?
options: The LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and it spoke to Balaam
The ass flew into the air
The ass disappeared suddenly
The ass turned into a man
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and it spoke to Balaam
questions.explanation: God opened the mouth of the ass, and it spoke, asking why Balaam had struck her three times (Numbers 22:28).

questions.question: What was Balaam’s response after seeing the angel of the LORD and realizing his mistake?
options: He admitted his sin and offered to return if it displeased the LORD
He ignored the angel and continued on
He cursed the ass for speaking
He fled back home immediately
questions.correctAnswer: He admitted his sin and offered to return if it displeased the LORD
questions.explanation: Balaam said he had sinned, not knowing the angel was there, and said he would return if it displeased the LORD (Numbers 22:34).

questions.question: What condition did the angel of the LORD place on Balaam when he was told to go with the princes again?
options: He must only speak the word that God puts in his mouth
He could curse or bless as he wished
He must not go at all
He must take the princes' rewards
questions.correctAnswer: He must only speak the word that God puts in his mouth
questions.explanation: The angel instructed Balaam to go but only speak the word God puts in his mouth (Numbers 22:35).

questions.question: True or False: Balaam said he had the power to speak anything he wanted when he came to Balak.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Balaam said he had no power to speak anything except the word God puts in his mouth (Numbers 22:38).

questions.question: True or False: Balak met Balaam at a city on the border of Arnon when he heard Balaam had come.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: When Balak heard Balaam had come, he went out to meet him at a city of Moab on the border of Arnon (Numbers 22:36).

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 22.

questions.question: What reason did Balaam give for striking his donkey three times?
options: Because the donkey mocked him
Because the donkey disobeyed his commands
Because the donkey refused to move
Because the donkey ran away
questions.correctAnswer: Because the donkey mocked him
questions.explanation: Balaam said to the ass, 'Because thou hast mocked me' after striking it three times (Numbers 22:29).

questions.question: What did the donkey say to Balaam when it miraculously spoke?
options: Am not I thine ass, upon which thou hast ridden ever since I was thine? Was I ever wont to do so unto thee?
Why do you strike me so often?
Shall I not carry you safely?
Do you not trust me?
questions.correctAnswer: Am not I thine ass, upon which thou hast ridden ever since I was thine? Was I ever wont to do so unto thee?
questions.explanation: The donkey questioned Balaam, reminding him of their long relationship and that it had never acted this way before (Numbers 22:30).

questions.question: What happened to Balaam after the LORD opened his eyes?
options: He saw the angel of the LORD standing with a drawn sword and fell flat on his face
He saw the armies of Moab approaching
He saw the children of Israel camping
He saw the donkey speaking again
questions.correctAnswer: He saw the angel of the LORD standing with a drawn sword and fell flat on his face
questions.explanation: After God opened Balaam's eyes, he saw the angel of the LORD with a sword drawn and fell flat on his face (Numbers 22:31).

questions.question: Why did the angel of the LORD say he went out to withstand Balaam?
options: Because Balaam’s way was perverse before God
Because Balaam was disobedient to Balak
Because Balaam was stealing from Moab
Because Balaam was afraid
questions.correctAnswer: Because Balaam’s way was perverse before God
questions.explanation: The angel declared he opposed Balaam because his way was perverse before the LORD (Numbers 22:32).

questions.question: What would have happened if the donkey had not turned away from the angel of the LORD?
options: Balaam would have been slain and the donkey saved alive
The donkey would have run away
Balaam would have been victorious in his journey
The angel would have disappeared
questions.correctAnswer: Balaam would have been slain and the donkey saved alive
questions.explanation: The angel said that unless the donkey turned away, Balaam would have been killed, but the donkey would have lived (Numbers 22:33).

questions.question: After realizing his sin, what did Balaam say to the angel of the LORD?
options: I have sinned; for I knew not that thou stoodest in the way against me
I will curse the people as you command
I will leave and never return
I will fight against the angel
questions.correctAnswer: I have sinned; for I knew not that thou stoodest in the way against me
questions.explanation: Balaam confessed his sin because he did not realize the angel stood in his way (Numbers 22:34).

questions.question: What instruction did the angel of the LORD give Balaam regarding his journey with the men from Moab?
options: Go with the men, but only speak the word God gives you
Refuse to go with the men at all costs
Curse the people as Balak requests
Take the men to a secret place
questions.correctAnswer: Go with the men, but only speak the word God gives you
questions.explanation: The angel told Balaam to go with the men but to speak only what God commands (Numbers 22:35).

questions.question: Where did Balak meet Balaam when he arrived in Moab?
options: To a city of Moab on the border of Arnon
In the plains of Moab by Jericho
At the high places of Baal
In Kirjathhuzoth
questions.correctAnswer: To a city of Moab on the border of Arnon
questions.explanation: Balak went out to meet Balaam at a city in Moab located on the border of Arnon (Numbers 22:36).

questions.question: What was Balaam’s response when Balak asked why he had delayed coming?
options: The word God puts in my mouth, that shall I speak
I was afraid to come
I was waiting for a larger reward
I did not want to curse Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The word God puts in my mouth, that shall I speak
questions.explanation: Balaam said he had no power to say anything except what God put in his mouth (Numbers 22:38).

questions.question: What city did Balaam and Balak come to after their meeting?
options: Kirjathhuzoth
Jericho
Pethor
Arnon
questions.correctAnswer: Kirjathhuzoth
questions.explanation: Balaam went with Balak and they came to Kirjathhuzoth (Numbers 22:39).

questions.question: What offerings did Balak present to Balaam upon his arrival?
options: Oxen and sheep
Gold and silver
Grain and wine
Goats and doves
questions.correctAnswer: Oxen and sheep
questions.explanation: Balak offered oxen and sheep to Balaam and the princes with him (Numbers 22:40).

questions.question: To what location did Balak take Balaam to view the Israelite camp?
options: The high places of Baal
The plains of Moab
The border of Arnon
Pethor
questions.correctAnswer: The high places of Baal
questions.explanation: Balak brought Balaam up to the high places of Baal to see the utmost part of the people (Numbers 22:41).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God restraining a prophet to only speak His word, as Balaam was instructed?
options: Jeremiah 1:9-10
Genesis 12:1-3
Exodus 3:10-12
Psalms 23
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 1:9-10
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 1:9-10 shows God placing His words in Jeremiah’s mouth and commanding him to speak only those words, paralleling Balaam’s instruction to only speak God’s word (Numbers 22:35).

questions.question: What is the significance of the donkey speaking in Hebrew tradition, and how does it relate to the original Hebrew word for 'ass' used here?
options: The Hebrew word 'חמור' (chamor) signifies a burden-bearer, and the speaking donkey symbolizes divine intervention through an ordinary creature
The Hebrew word means 'wild beast' and the donkey represents chaos
The word means 'fast runner' and symbolizes swiftness
The word means 'stubborn one' and the donkey symbolizes obstinacy
questions.correctAnswer: The Hebrew word 'חמור' (chamor) signifies a burden-bearer, and the speaking donkey symbolizes divine intervention through an ordinary creature
questions.explanation: The word 'ass' is 'חמור' (chamor) in Hebrew, implying a beast of burden. The donkey speaking highlights God’s power to use the ordinary to reveal His message (Numbers 22:28-30).

questions.question: Which literary device best describes the narrative structure involving Balaam, his donkey, and the angel in this chapter?
options: Chiasm
Simile
Parable
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The episode reveals a chiasm structure: Balaam’s journey is interrupted by divine opposition (angel), the donkey’s unusual behavior, and Balaam’s enlightenment—symmetrical elements highlighting God's control (Numbers 22:22-35).

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was Balak’s main reason for sending messengers to Balaam according to Numbers 22:5-6?
options: To bless the children of Israel
To curse the children of Israel to overcome and drive them out
To invite Balaam to a feast
To seek Balaam's advice on war tactics
questions.correctAnswer: To curse the children of Israel to overcome and drive them out
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:5-6 explains that Balak sent messengers to Balaam to curse the people of Israel because they were too mighty for him, hoping to prevail over them and drive them out of the land.

questions.question: According to Numbers 22:12, what reason does God give Balaam for refusing to let him curse Israel?
options: Because Balaam was not a true prophet
Because the people were blessed
Because Balak was not a righteous king
Because Balaam had not been paid yet
questions.correctAnswer: Because the people were blessed
questions.explanation: In Numbers 22:12, God tells Balaam not to curse the Israelites because they are blessed, indicating God's sovereign blessing upon His chosen people.

questions.question: What does Balaam’s statement in Numbers 22:18 reveal about his view of prophetic authority?
options: He can act independently of God's word
He must obey only Balak's commands
He cannot go beyond the word of the LORD to do less or more
He can choose whether to obey God or not
questions.correctAnswer: He cannot go beyond the word of the LORD to do less or more
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:18 shows Balaam’s acknowledgment that prophetic authority is bound strictly to the word of God, emphasizing divine sovereignty over human will.

questions.question: What divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in God’s interaction with Balaam in Numbers 22:20?
options: God’s omniscience
God’s patience
God’s sovereignty and guidance
God’s wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty and guidance
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:20 shows God giving specific instructions to Balaam, demonstrating His sovereign control over human actions and His guidance in fulfilling His purposes.

questions.question: How does the episode of Balaam’s donkey speaking in Numbers 22:28-30 contribute to the narrative’s theological message?
options: It shows animals are more faithful than humans
It illustrates God’s use of unexpected means to communicate His will
It proves Balaam was insane
It indicates Balaam’s donkey was possessed
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God’s use of unexpected means to communicate His will
questions.explanation: In Numbers 22:28-30, God opens the mouth of the donkey to speak to Balaam, demonstrating that God can use surprising and miraculous methods to reveal His message and correct human behavior.

questions.question: What does Balaam’s reaction after seeing the angel in Numbers 22:31-34 reveal about human sinfulness and divine justice?
options: Balaam was intentionally rebellious
Balaam immediately repents and acknowledges his sin
Balaam refuses to admit fault
Balaam blames the donkey for his troubles
questions.correctAnswer: Balaam immediately repents and acknowledges his sin
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:34 shows Balaam confessing his sin, illustrating human fallibility and the justice of God who confronts and corrects disobedience.

questions.question: According to Numbers 22:35, what limitation does God impose on Balaam’s prophetic mission?
options: Balaam must only speak the word God gives him
Balaam can only bless the people
Balaam can travel anywhere he wishes
Balaam must not meet Balak
questions.correctAnswer: Balaam must only speak the word God gives him
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:35 commands Balaam to speak only the word God gives him, emphasizing the divine control over prophetic speech and the importance of obedience to God’s revealed will.

questions.question: How does Balak’s response to Balaam’s arrival in Numbers 22:36-37 reflect human misunderstanding of divine authority?
options: Balak recognizes Balaam’s independence
Balak expects Balaam to curse Israel at his command
Balak respects Balaam’s relationship with God
Balak doubts the power of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Balak expects Balaam to curse Israel at his command
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:36-37 shows Balak questioning why Balaam delayed and assuming he could command Balaam to curse Israel, reflecting a misunderstanding of God’s sovereign authority over prophecy.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s blessing and curse is taught by the dialogue in Numbers 22:6 and Numbers 22:12?
options: People can manipulate God’s blessings by their actions
God’s blessings and curses are conditional on human will
Whoever God blesses is blessed and whoever He curses is cursed, regardless of human attempts
God changes His mind according to Balaam’s decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Whoever God blesses is blessed and whoever He curses is cursed, regardless of human attempts
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:6 and 22:12 together affirm that divine blessing and curse are sovereign acts of God, not subject to human manipulation, underscoring His ultimate authority over nations.

questions.question: What theological insight about God’s justice and mercy can be synthesized from Numbers 22:22 and Numbers 22:33?
options: God punishes Balaam without warning
God’s justice is tempered by mercy, sparing Balaam’s life while correcting his way
God ignores human disobedience
God allows Balaam to proceed freely without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice is tempered by mercy, sparing Balaam’s life while correcting his way
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:22 shows God’s anger and the angel opposing Balaam, while 22:33 reveals the angel’s mercy in sparing Balaam’s life, illustrating the balance of divine justice and mercy.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Balaam and the donkey (Numbers 22:21-33) contribute to the doctrine of divine providence?
options: It shows that God is indifferent to human decisions
It reveals God’s active involvement in guiding and restraining human actions for His purposes
It suggests that animals have authority over humans
It teaches that prophetic missions are always successful
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals God’s active involvement in guiding and restraining human actions for His purposes
questions.explanation: The story in Numbers 22:21-33 illustrates divine providence as God intervenes supernaturally to direct Balaam’s journey and prevent him from sinning, demonstrating God’s control over history and individuals.

questions.question: What Christological foreshadowing is present in the role of the angel of the LORD in Numbers 22:31-35?
options: The angel represents Christ as the divine mediator confronting sin and guiding obedience
The angel is a mere human messenger
The angel symbolizes an enemy of Israel
The angel foretells the coming of a priest
questions.correctAnswer: The angel represents Christ as the divine mediator confronting sin and guiding obedience
questions.explanation: The angel of the LORD in Numbers 22:31-35 acts with divine authority, confronting Balaam’s sin and directing him, typologically pointing to Christ as the divine mediator who deals with sin and leads obedience (cf. John 1:18, Hebrews 1:3).

questions.question: Considering Numbers 22:1-4, how does the fear of Moab and Midian reflect the broader redemptive narrative concerning Israel’s promised inheritance?
options: It shows Israel’s weakness and vulnerability
It highlights the fulfillment of God’s promise to multiply Israel and establish them in the land
It indicates that Israel was not yet chosen
It reveals God's rejection of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the fulfillment of God’s promise to multiply Israel and establish them in the land
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:1-4 depicts Moab’s fear because Israel is numerous and powerful, demonstrating the unfolding of God’s promise to Abraham that his descendants would inherit the land and be a great nation (Genesis 12:2-3).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from Numbers 22:8 and Numbers 22:20 regarding divine revelation and human response?
options: God reveals His will only once
Human response is irrelevant to divine revelation
God communicates His will progressively, and human obedience depends on hearing and acting on His word
Divine revelation is always ambiguous
questions.correctAnswer: God communicates His will progressively, and human obedience depends on hearing and acting on His word
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:8 shows Balaam inviting the princes to stay while he seeks God’s word, and 22:20 records God giving further instructions, illustrating that revelation unfolds progressively and human obedience must follow accordingly.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the story of Balaam’s talking donkey is a myth with no theological value. What does Numbers 22:21-33 actually teach about God’s sovereignty and intervention in human affairs?
options: It supports the idea that God sometimes uses miraculous signs to redirect human will and uphold His purposes
It proves that animals have divine powers
It is merely a parable with no historical basis
It suggests that God does not intervene in human sin
questions.correctAnswer: It supports the idea that God sometimes uses miraculous signs to redirect human will and uphold His purposes
questions.explanation: Numbers 22:21-33 demonstrates God’s sovereignty by intervening supernaturally through the donkey and the angel to correct Balaam’s path, affirming divine providence and active involvement in human history.
